newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: SOCCER-LANUS WIN CONMEBOL TO GIVE ARGENTINA CLEAN SWEEP.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-LANUS WIN CONMEBOL TO GIVE ARGENTINA CLEAN SWEEP.

text.p: Lanus gave Argentina a clean sweep of the three South American club competitions on Wednesday when they won the Conmebol Cup despite going down 1-0 to Santa Fe of Colombia in the second leg of the final.

Lanus, an unfashionable club from a Buenos Aires suburb who had never previously won either a domestic or international trophy, took the title thanks to a 2-0 win at home in the first leg two weeks ago.
Santa Fe, with a two-goal deficit to make up, got off to the perfect start when Francisco Whittingham scored from the penalty spot in the third minute after having been fouled himself.
Backed by a 50,000 crowd at the Campin stadium, Santa Fe dominated the game but their attacks frequently broke down around the edge of the Argentine penalty area.
In the second half, Lanus goalkeeper Carlos Roa made three superb saves.

Earlier on Wednesday, Lanus' compatriots Velez Sarsfield won the South American Supercup, which is played every year between previous Libertadores winners, by beating Cruzeiro of Brazil 2-0 for a 3-0 aggregate win.
In June, River Plate won the Libertadores, the continent's premier club competition, after overcoming America, another Colombian side, in the final.
Santa Fe were once a power in Colombian soccer but have not won anything since the last of their six domestic titles in 1975.
The Conmebol was started in 1992 and is run roughly along the lines of Europe's Uefa Cup. It has been won three times by Brazilian clubs and twice by Argentines.
